newsitem.title: SWEDEN: MoDo Paper sees lasting upturn in trends.
newsitem.headline: MoDo Paper sees lasting upturn in trends.

text.p: MoDo Paper, a unit of Swedish forestry group MoDo, said on Wednesday it saw a lasting upturn in forestry trends.
"We share U.S. companies' view that the global pulp market is strong, mainly in the U.S.," MoDo Paper president Hans Pettersson told Reuters.
"We think we are now at a point when (forestry trends) will turn upwards."
Pettersson referred to very strong market trends for short-fibre pulp.
"The short-fibre market is even stronger than long-fibre and this is usually a sign that (trends) will turn," he said.

Several Swedish pulp producers have said three U.S. pulp makers -- Weyerhaeuser, Stone Container and Georgia Pacific -- are believed to have announced a price rise on long-fibre pulp to $630 a tonne from $580.
Pettersson did not say MoDo would follow suit, but said he shared the U.S. groups' market view.
